# `Q-2-35` — Invalid List-Table Structure

> A `::: {.list-table}` div does not contain a well-formed
> list-table source, so Quarto cannot convert it into a table.

## What this means

Quarto's recommended way to write tables is a *list-table*: a
fenced div with class `list-table` whose body is a nested
markdown list, where each top-level list item is a row and each
nested list item is a cell.

This error fires when the parser finds a `list-table` div but
its body is not a list at all, or its list does not have the
structure a list-table requires (rows with consistent cell
counts).

## Why this happens

Common shapes that trigger the error:

- The body is plain text, not a list.
- The body is a list, but rows have different numbers of cells.
- Nesting is wrong — the cells are listed at the same level as
  the rows.

The same check runs on a `list-table` div that an `{lmd}` cell
builds from nodes (`pandoc.Div({ … }, pandoc.Attr("", {"list-table"}))`),
or that `pandoc.read` returns. A node built in a cell has no
position of its own in the document, so the warning then points at
the cell's code and says the node was built there.

## How to fix

Restructure the body so that each top-level list item is a row
and each nested list item is one cell:

```markdown
::: {.list-table}
- - Header 1
  - Header 2
- - Cell A
  - Cell B
- - Cell C
  - Cell D
:::
```

Use exactly the same number of cells in every row.

  the recommended alternative.
